headline: Growth hormone and IGF-1
body: People treat them as one axis with two names.
punch: They act on different stages of the same cell lineage.

headline: The simple model
body: Growth hormone hits the liver, the liver makes IGF-1, IGF-1 does the growing. Clean, popular, and incomplete.
punch: There's direct in vivo evidence against it, from 1994.

headline: The experiment
body: Hypophysectomised rats — no endogenous pituitary hormone at all — then infused either GH or IGF-1 separately. No confounds, one variable at a time.
punch: The cleanest possible separation of the two.

headline: Growth hormone
body: GH primarily pulls resting-zone chondrocytes into the proliferative pool. It decides how many cells enter the production line.

headline: IGF-1
body: IGF-1 acts on cells already proliferating, driving their expansion. It decides how much each recruited cell produces.
punch: IGF-1 sets how far each one goes.

headline: Which is why
body: Recruiting more cells and expanding existing ones are different operations. Maximising one does not substitute for the other, and neither alone reproduces normal growth.
punch: Two levers, two functions, one lineage.

headline: And it broke
body: This was among the earliest direct in vivo evidence that GH acts locally at the growth plate, not merely by raising circulating IGF-1 from the liver.
punch: A dual local-action model, demonstrated in 1994.

headline: Which modern work
body: GH acts directly on human growth plate stem cells through JAK/STAT and local TGF-beta, independent of the liver IGF-1 axis. Same conclusion, thirty years later.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
